parole.significato: A person from Denmark or of Danish descent.
parole.testo: From Middle English Dane, from Old Norse danir or Old English Dene. Both forms ultimately descend from Proto-Germanic *daniz.

parole.significato: A temple, sanctuary, a shrine, or hall.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old Norse hof or Old English hof, reinforced in modern (post-1990, chiefly neopagan) use by Icelandic hof (“shrine, temple”).

parole.significato: A harsh, high-pitched sound or cry (as of a hawk).
parole.testo: Onomatopoeic. However, some connection to a lost dialect term (Old Norse influence? cf. shriek, screech) from Old English sċrēon is not impossible.

parole.significato: To walk proudly; to sweep along.
parole.testo: From Middle English swaipen (“to strike, scourge”), from Old Norse sveipa (“to sweep, stroke”) and/or Old English swāpan (“to sweep”); both ultimately from Proto-Germanic *swaipaną (“to sweep, swing, hurl, fling”). Doublet of swoop.

parole.significato: Scandinavian/Northern European seafarers, most familiarly raiders and pirates during the Viking age.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Old Norse víkingr (“Viking”).
